<!-- pr-reviewer: 46815caa8ff6b5692caecfad845883aeb4e02794 -->
**Needs changes before merge** (merge conflict with main; one wrong status message)

The conversion and undo design are right; two items to fix.

**Requested before merge**
1. Merge conflict with main in code: `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs` - both branches add a `mod` line to the list near `mod face_origin;`. Please merge `origin/main` and keep both `mod` lines (ledger `RECOMMENDED.md` also conflicts; keep both sides).
2. Wrong status text for a zero diameter: `crates/ui/src/egui_app/spindle_row.rs:93-94`. With a tool diameter of 0 in surface mode, `rpm_for` returns `None` and the arm says `spindle speed not changed: it must be above zero`, which blames the speed, not the diameter. The refusal itself is correct (no command is queued). Suggest a diameter-specific message, e.g. `tool diameter must be above zero to show or set surface speed`.

**What looks good**
- Conversion checked: m/min = pi·D·n/1000 with D in mm; SFM = pi·(D/25.4)·n/12; the inverses round-trip. 1/2" at 1000 rpm = 130.9 SFM. Pinned by `surface_speed_and_rpm_invert_in_both_units`.
- Posted S is unchanged for existing projects: the post still reads `Tool::rpm`, the rpm/surface switch is view state (`State::spindle_as_vc`, not saved), and no project format changes.
- Undo: a committed value is one `ChangeTool`; its `invert` restores the captured `prev`. A drag commits once on release, not per frame (`spindle_row.rs:77`, draft in egui temp memory).
- A same or non-positive speed is no command (`set_rpm`), pinned by `a_new_speed_is_one_change_tool_and_a_same_or_bad_one_is_none`.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
- Machine limit: the row accepts up to 200 000 rpm (`spindle_row.rs:77`) regardless of the machine's `spindle_max`. The app already refuses over-limit spindle speeds at check time by name (`crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs:155`, `cutting.rs:182`), so nothing gouges silently. Showing the machine limit on the row, or clamping to it, would be a nicer UX.
- Scope: the speed lives on the tool, so editing it changes every operation using that tool. The hover says so, and the request asked for `EditOperationParams`; `ChangeTool` is the command that owns tool data, so I accept it. A per-operation override is correctly left for its own issue.

**Local results**
- Trial merge with `origin/main`: conflict in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs` (code). Per the review rules the PR head was reviewed without merging.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --no-fail-fast` in `crates/ui` at the PR head: all green.
  - lib: 245 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored
  - boundary 3, boundary_picks 6, edge_loop_pick 2, egui_app 3, feedback 6, fixtures 7, gpu_render 9, machine 6, models 4, operations 31, shell 19, theme_files 14, trace_composite 4, trace_parity 5
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 40fd7ba065d886e7ab8e45ccc2329fdef10c576d -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge**

Thanks, bherbruck. The earlier findings are addressed.

**What looks good**
- Diameter-specific refusal: `refusal()` (spindle_row.rs) names a zero or non-finite tool diameter as the cause in surface mode. A bad rpm still gets the generic "must be above zero" message. Pinned by `a_zero_diameter_is_named_as_the_cause_in_surface_mode`.
- Hold to the machine maximum: `hold_to_machine()` clamps a committed speed to `spindle_max` (floored) and sets a status note: "spindle speed N rpm held to the machine's maximum M". The user is told, so it is not silent. The row's hover also states the maximum. Pinned by `a_speed_over_the_machine_maximum_is_held_to_it`.
- The check-time refusal is untouched. `crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs:155` still flags `tool.rpm > spindle_max`, so a tool edited elsewhere or a machine swapped later is still refused.
- Holding is safe. It can only lower the commanded speed to a value the machine states it can run. A missing or non-positive `spindle_max` leaves the value as typed, so the check-time refusal stays the backstop.
- Original design points hold:
  - m/min and SFM conversions round-trip in both units (`surface_speed_and_rpm_invert_in_both_units`).
  - The post still reads `Tool::rpm`.
  - `spindle_as_vc` is view state on `State` and is not saved.
  - A commit is a single `ChangeTool` (`set_rpm`), and the same speed produces no command. The commit builds a `Tool` from the old one, so undo restores the prior rpm.
  - A drag keeps its draft in egui temp memory and commits once on release, Enter or focus loss.
- The merge from main is clean. The RECOMMENDED entry now lives in `docs/decisions/225-spindle-edit.md`. The `tests.rs` mod lines are kept.
- The module has a provenance line, no `unwrap()` or `panic!` outside tests, and no new dependencies.

**Local results (PR merged with current origin/main, Windows)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (from `crates/ui`) | 275 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored |
| the 5 spindle tests (4 unit tests plus the Feeds-tab UI test) | all pass |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

The diff touches only `crates/ui/src` (plus the decisions doc), so I did not run the ui integration binaries under `crates/ui/tests`.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. The hold uses the machine active at commit time. The tool is shared by every operation that uses it, so another setup on a different machine could still trip the check-time refusal. That refusal is the intended backstop.
2. The hold ignores `spindle_min`. A low value is still caught at check time.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
